SUMMARY Management reported that Akamai Technologies, Inc. ( AKAM +2.94% ) is transitioning to a primary infrastructure provider for the AI economy, leveraging its distributed global platform to secure and deliver agentic workloads. The company signed $2.8 billion in multiyear cloud infrastructure commitments year to date, including a significant new robotics contract, which provides long term revenue visibility. Akamai stated that its top-line revenue growth is expected to accelerate to the low teens in 2027 as these large scale deployments ramp up. To support this growth, management is reallocating capital from share repurchases to a $500 million GPU expansion program. Furthermore, the company completed the acquisition of LayerX to address the security requirements of enterprise employees interacting with generative AI tools. CEO Leighton noted that the infrastructure for AI agents will be a "flexible continuum" stretching from the core data center to the network edge for low latency processing. CFO McGowan reported that all current GPU capacity is "completely sold out," necessitating an additional $500 million investment to meet the robust pipeline for 2027. Management confirmed that CrowdStrike, an AI native cybersecurity platform, switched to Akamai for its web security and content delivery needs in a competitive win. Large scale CIS contracts are structured with "take or pay commitments" to ensure attractive cash flow profiles despite significant upfront capital requirements. Leighton indicated that the company is participating in the Open Secure AI Alliance to assist major enterprises in securing critical infrastructure against AI enhanced threats. The company was selected as a strategic partner in WWT's AI Readiness Model for Operational Resilience to protect large scale AI clusters from lateral threat movement. Leighton attributed the success of the cloud portfolio to the platform's distribution in 700 cities and 130 countries, which reduces latency and egress costs for customers. INDUSTRY GLOSSARY API Security : Technology used to protect Application Programming Interfaces from unauthorized access, misuse, or cyberattacks. CIS (Cloud Infrastructure Services) : Akamai's portfolio of cloud computing, storage, and networking solutions. GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) : Specialized hardware used for intensive computational tasks, including AI training and inference. Inference : The process of using a trained AI model to make predictions or execute tasks based on new data. Microsegmentation : A security method that divides a network into small, isolated zones to prevent attackers from moving laterally. WAF (Web Application Firewall) : A security solution that filters and monitors HTTP traffic between a web application and the internet. Zero Trust : A security framework that requires all users and devices to be continuously authenticated and authorized before gaining access to applications or data.
